server.description: How the HTTP listener is bound and what the transport accepts.

engine.description: Where `catalog-engine` is reached, and how patiently.

auth.description: The identity posture and the canonical resource identifiers.

tools.description: What bounds a tool call and what the tool set advertises.

response.description: How a tool result is rendered.

observability.description: What the server reports about itself.

ServerConfig.description:
How the HTTP listener is bound and what the transport accepts (§11).

`allowed_hosts` has **no usable default**: the SDK's own default is loopback-only, so a
remote deployment answers every request `403 Forbidden: Host header is not allowed` until
the list is set. Validation therefore refuses an empty list before the listener binds (D11).

mcpPath.description: Path the MCP service is mounted at.

allowedHosts.description:
Hostnames or `host:port` authorities accepted in the inbound `Host` header.
Required and non-empty — see the type documentation.

allowedOrigins.description:
Browser origins accepted in the inbound `Origin` header. Empty leaves `Origin`
validation switched off, which is what the in-cluster client needs (D11).

maxBodyBytes.description: Maximum accepted POST body size, in bytes.

EngineConfig.description:
Where `catalog-engine` is reached, and how patiently (§11).

`base_url` always points at the **API gateway**, never at the engine `Service`: every
outbound call has to traverse `ext_authz` so the server can never do more than its caller
could do itself (D27, D48). Validation refuses a `base_url` that addresses the engine
directly.

baseUrl.description: Base URL of the API gateway in front of `catalog-engine`.

apiPrefix.description: Path prefix the gateway routes `catalog-engine` behind.

timeoutMs.description: Per-request timeout against the engine, in milliseconds.

connectTimeoutMs.description: Connect timeout against the engine, in milliseconds.

maxRetries.description: Maximum retry attempts for a request the §8.1 policy classifies as retryable.

AuthConfig.description:
The identity posture and the canonical resource identifiers (§7.3).

The Protected Resource Metadata document is served by Envoy, not by this process, so
`resource` exists to match Envoy's string exactly rather than to be published from here.

mode.description: What the server does with the caller's identity.

resource.description: The canonical resource URI, matching the `resource` value Envoy publishes.

resourceMetadataUrl.description: The URL of the Protected Resource Metadata document Envoy serves.

AuthMode.description:
What the server does with the caller's identity (§7.2).

`ResourceServer` is accepted by the schema — the value and this variant exist so the
decision is additive — but **refused by validation in v1** (D46): starting up and silently
behaving as `Gateway` is how a trust boundary quietly stops existing.

oneOf.description: Extract, never reject: the gateway has already authenticated and authorized (D47).
Validate the bearer token ourselves. Not implemented in v1 — see P-C3.

ToolsConfig.description:
What bounds a tool call and what the tool set advertises (§11).

`tools_list_ttl_ms` sits here rather than under `transport` because it is a property of the
tool set (D13), not of the wire.

callDeadlineSeconds.description: Wall-clock budget for one `tools/call`, in seconds.

RateLimitConfig.description:
The per-tenant token bucket of §6.4. Buckets are per replica, so the effective cluster
limit is `replicas × rate`.

**Off by default in v1**: it limits nothing unless `enabled` is set to `true`.

enabled.description: Whether the limiter runs at all.

perTenantCallsPerMinute.description: Refill rate, in calls per minute, per tenant.

ToolDefaults.description:
Every tunable the tool analyses marked as a guess (§11). They live here, not in the code,
because the measurement exercise will change them and a config change is not a release.

**No response ceilings are among them** — there are none (D34).

complianceWaitSeconds.description: How long a compliance evaluation is waited on, in seconds.

maxWriteBytes.description: Ceiling on the bytes a caller may send us in one write.

ResponseConfig.description:
How a tool result is rendered (§11).

`structured_content` stays **off** (D15): returning every result twice — as text and as
structured content — doubles the metric this project exists to reduce. It is a switch, not
a design choice, so a client that needs it can have it without a release.

TransportConfig.description:
The SDK transport knobs, every one of them read from configuration rather than hardcoded
(§6.1).

`legacy_session_mode` stays **on** because our only client today is handshake-era (D2);
requests that negotiate `2026-07-28` are served statelessly regardless. `json_response`
only *prefers* JSON — the transport falls back to SSE by itself when a handler emits a
notification before its result (D9).

legacySessionMode.description: Whether handshake-era sessions are created and tracked.

jsonResponse.description: Whether a single JSON response is preferred over an SSE stream.

HealthConfig.description:
What `/-/ready` checks (D43).

`/-/healthz` takes nothing from here: liveness never calls the engine, because a dependency
outage must not get the pod restarted.

readinessChecksEngine.description: Whether readiness also probes the engine.

engineProbeTimeoutMs.description: Timeout for that probe, in milliseconds.

ObservabilityConfig.description: What the server reports about itself (§10).
